subject: Atlas Health — commercial terms and invoice/tax routing
messages:
From: Jason Sullivan <j.sullivan@atlashealth.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft redlines: Order Form (pricing, min commit, invoicing)

Hi Kimberly / Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to share our redlines for the Order Form and call out two items that need clarification before we move to PO:

1) Pricing schedule: We noticed the committed token tiers in Appendix A appear to assume quarterly tranches. We need the price table to reflect monthly phasing (Q1/Q2 ramp footprint). Can you confirm pricing per token for month 1 vs steady state month?

2) Minimum commitment: Atlas needs a 12-month minimum commitment with a graduated ramp. Can you accept an annual minimum with a 25% ramp in Q1?

3) Net terms & invoicing: Procurement is requesting Net-30 payment and PO acceptance prior to invoice. Also want invoices addressed to: Accounts Payable, Atlas Health, 123 Meridian Ave, San Francisco, CA.

4) Taxes: Atlas will provide a US tax-exempt certificate for state sales tax where applicable. We also need clarity whether Redwood applies any withholding on cross-border payments (we are a US entity, but some Suppliers ask).

Attached are our redlines (Atlas_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.pdf). Can you confirm whether these items require MSA-level changes or if they can be handled at the Order Form level?

Best,
Jason Sullivan
Procurement Manager | Atlas Health
procurement@atlashealth.com

--
Attachment: Atlas_OrderForm_Redlines_v1.pdf (application/pdf, 128 KB)
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Jason Sullivan <j.sullivan@atlashealth.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft redlines: Order Form (pricing, min commit, invoicing)

Jason —

Thanks for sending these over and for the clear asks. High-level responses below; legal will flag anything that needs MSA edits, but my read is most changes can be contained to the Order Form / Appendix.

- Pricing schedule: We can produce a month-by-month breakout. I’ve asked Camila to prepare a payment matrix showing month 1 vs steady-state per-token pricing and effective dates.

- Minimum commitment: We’re generally comfortable with a 12-month minimum if the ramp is clearly captured in Appendix A. Need to confirm the billing cadence for a ramped commit — do you want invoices to reflect actual usage each month with true-ups?

- Net terms & invoicing: Redwood standard is Net-30 for most agreements; we can accept Net-30. PO acceptance is fine — our finance team needs the PO number on invoices. Please confirm the AP contact name and PO routing.

- Taxes: If you provide a state sales-tax exemption certificate we will exclude state sales tax where applicable. Redwood does not withhold on domestic US payments; if Atlas is making payments from a non-US entity we’ll need to review.

I’ve looped Ben (Sales Ops / Contract Liaison) to coordinate the redline pass and legal counters. Expect a draft response and a revised Order Form (for signature via DocuSign) by end of day Wednesday.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft redlines: Order Form (pricing, min commit, invoicing)

Jason —

I reviewed Atlas’s PDF and put together line-by-line commercial/legal notes. Quick summary of the items that would trigger MSA modifications vs Order Form-only edits:

- Pricing & Appendix A: Order Form only — we will produce a month-by-month price table. We will add a short definition of "Steady State" in Appendix A to avoid ambiguity.

- Minimum commitment: Order Form only if Atlas accepts our standard remedy for early termination (pro-rated true-up of remaining committed spend at applicable tiered rate). If Atlas requests different termination liability language, that will touch the MSA.

- Net terms & PO: Order Form only — we will add PO field and billing address block.

- Taxes & Withholding: This is MSA-adjacent. Any language that shifts tax indemnity or requires Redwood to gross-up payments for Atlas withholding needs legal review. As noted, for US-to-US we don't apply withholding. If Atlas confirms US entity and provides a tax-exempt certificate, that's straightforward.

I attached a redline summary (bulleted) inside the PDF I sent to Kimberly. For tracking, please assign a single redline owner on Atlas's side so we can iterate quickly.

Regards,
Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
